# 30-day plan to double from 140 to 280 subscribers

Doubling in 30 days means about 140 new subscribers in 4 Saturdays, with no churn. That's possible but hard. Most realistic plans would land somewhere around +50 to +90. The plan below gives you a real shot at 280. The timing helps: it's 19 November, so the next 30 days run straight into Christmas, and that's your biggest lever.

## Step 0 (this week): check you can deliver 280 boxes
Before you sell anything, confirm you can **bake and deliver** twice as many boxes on a Saturday morning with 3 people and cargo bikes. Selling more than you can deliver would hurt you more than slow growth.
- How many boxes can one bike run carry, and how many runs fit before about 11:00?
- Options if you're short: a second bike for December, a part-time rider, a pickup option at the shop (for example with a small discount), or a Friday-evening delivery slot.
- Decide the cap now. If capacity is 220, aim for 220 and start a waitlist after that. A waitlist also makes the box look in demand.

## 1. Gift subscriptions (target: +40 to +60)
This is the biggest opportunity and it comes from timing.
- Sell "4 Saturdays of bread" for €72 and "12 weeks" for about €200, with the first box delivered in January. Add a printed card the buyer can put under the tree.
- Sell them at the till, on your website and in every box you deliver this month.
- After the gift ends, recipients convert to paying subscribers at a decent rate, so January gets a second wave.
- Note that these are prepaid gifts. Count them separately from recurring subscribers when you report on the goal.

## 2. Referrals from your 140 subscribers (target: +30 to +45)
Your current subscribers already live in your delivery area and trust you.
- Offer: "Give a friend their first box free, and you get a free box when they stay for a second week."
- The reward costs you ingredients and labour, not €18 in cash, so it's cheap compared with ads.
- Put 2 printed invite cards with a unique code in every box for the next 4 Saturdays, and email or message all subscribers once a week.
- Personally ask your 20 most loyal subscribers. Even a handful of enthusiastic ones can bring in several people each.

## 3. Turn shop customers into subscribers (target: +25 to +40)
People who already buy at the counter are your warmest prospects.
- Ask every customer at the till: "Do you live within 3 km? We deliver every Saturday." Track how many you ask and how many sign up.
- Offer a **€9 first box** (half price) with sign-up by QR code on the spot.
- Run a tasting on Saturday or Sunday mornings showing what goes in this week's box.

## 4. Local saturation within 3 km (target: +20 to +30, spending most of the €300)
- **Flyers** (about €120): one targeted drop to the densest streets on your existing delivery routes, since added boxes there cost almost nothing to deliver. Include the €9 trial code.
- **Neighbourhood groups** (free): Facebook, WhatsApp, Nextdoor-style groups and school parent groups. Post real photos from the bakery at 5am, not ads.
- **Partnerships** (free to €100): co-working spaces, gyms, yoga studios and nearby offices. Offer them a sample tray in exchange for promoting you to their members with a group code. One office signing up 8 people does more than 500 flyers.
- **Local press or Instagram creators**: "neighbourhood bakery delivers by cargo bike" is an easy story for a local news site.

## 5. Protect the base (avoid losing 5 to 10)
Losing subscribers while you grow means you have to go faster just to stand still.
- Add a "pause for holidays" option so December travel doesn't turn into cancellations.
- Put a small extra treat in every box in December. It costs little and gets people talking about you.

## Weekly rhythm
| Week | Focus |
|---|---|
| 1 (now) | Capacity check, launch gift subscriptions, print referral and flyer materials, set up codes |
| 2 | Flyer drop, till script live, first partnership pitches, referral cards in boxes |
| 3 | Push gift subscriptions hard, run the tasting weekend, follow up partnerships |
| 4 | Last call for Christmas gifts, personal referral asks, start the January waitlist |

Track three numbers every Monday: new subscribers by channel, cancellations, and Saturday capacity used.

## My honest view
I'd treat **280 as the stretch goal and about 220 recurring plus gift subscriptions as a strong result**. I'd measure the plan against that rather than against doubling. Pushing for 280 at any cost risks discounting too much and late or failed deliveries, and that would undo the growth.

To sharpen the numbers it would help to know:
1. How many boxes you can realistically bake and deliver on one Saturday today.
2. Roughly how many non-subscriber customers come into the shop each week.
3. How many subscribers you lose in a typical month.
